HIST 101.description: The rise and development of European civilization from its Mediterranean origins through the Renaissance and Reformation.
HIST 101.subject: HIST
HIST 101.title: European Civilization from Ancient Times to the Mid-17th Century

HIST 102.description: European development and expansion from the mid-17th century to the present.
HIST 102.subject: HIST
HIST 102.title: European Civilization from the Mid-17th Century

HIST 103.description: Political, cultural, and economic forces that have conditioned the development of institutions and ideas in South Asia.
HIST 103.subject: HIST
HIST 103.title: Introduction to South Asian History

HIST 104.description: An analysis which treats the major cultural elements of traditional Islamic civilization and then concentrates upon the reactions of the Arabs, Turks, and Iranians to the problems of adjusting to the modern world.
HIST 104.subject: HIST
HIST 104.title: Introduction to the Civilization of the Islamic Middle East

HIST 105.description: The evolution of social, political, and cultural patterns in East Asia, with emphasis on the development of philosophical, religious, and political institutions and their relationship to literary and artistic forms in China and Japan.
HIST 105.subject: HIST
HIST 105.title: Introduction to East Asian Civilization

HIST 106.description: An examination of several traditional sub-Saharan African societies and of their political and economic transformation in the modern, colonial, and post-independence periods.
HIST 106.subject: HIST
HIST 106.title: Introduction to African History

HIST 107.description: The political, social, religious, economic, military, and intellectual development of Ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia, and adjoining areas from the origins of civilization until the seventh century A.D.
HIST 107.subject: HIST
HIST 107.title: Introduction to Ancient Near Eastern Civilization

HIST 108.description: The development of science and technology and their roles in world civilizations from antiquity to the present.
HIST 108.subject: HIST
HIST 108.title: Science and Technology in World History

HIST 109.description: A discussion of the political, cultural, and economic forces which have conditioned the development of institutions and ideas in Spanish and Portuguese America.
HIST 109.subject: HIST
HIST 109.title: Introduction to Latin American Civilization

HIST 110.description: Comparative examination of conquest, colonization, and human captivity in the history, cultural values, and social ethics of European, African, and Indigenous civilizations in the Americas, 1441-1888.
HIST 110.subject: HIST
HIST 110.title: Conquest, Colonization, and Captivity: A Cultural History of the Americas from 1441 to 1888

HIST 111.description: A general survey of the United States from the era of discovery to 1865, emphasizing major political, economic, social, and intellectual developments.
HIST 111.subject: HIST
HIST 111.title: United States History to 1865

HIST 112.description: A general survey of the United States from 1865 to the present, emphasizing major political, economic, social, and intellectual developments. Honors sections are available for students in the honors program.
HIST 112.subject: HIST
HIST 112.title: United States History since 1865

HIST 201.description: Introduction to Declaration of independence, Constitution, Federalist Papers, Bill of Rights, landmark Supreme Court cases and constitutional amendments; exploration of these texts’ historical context and debates about their meaning.
HIST 201.subject: HIST
HIST 201.title: American Founding Documents

HIST 205.description: Origins and development of capitalism in Europe and the United States from the Renaissance to the Modern Period, with attention to modern historical studies and primary sources including Adam Smith, Karl Marx, and Max Weber.
HIST 205.subject: HIST
HIST 205.title: Origins of Capitalism

HIST 206.description: An introduction to Western legal history with a view to its foundations in ancient Roman law and the influence of the English common law on modern legal systems including that of the United States.
HIST 206.subject: HIST
HIST 206.title: History of Law

HIST 209.description: History of magic as theory and practice from antiquity to modernity and beyond. Chronological, geographical, and thematic range stretches from ancient Mesopotamia, Greece, and Rome; to the Jewish, Christian, and Islamic worlds; to early modernity and the modern period in Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas.
HIST 209.subject: HIST
HIST 209.title: History of Magic

HIST 213.description: The history and development of an American region, “the West,” through the narratives of its diverse people and the effects of its complex geography.
HIST 213.subject: HIST
HIST 213.title: History of the American West

HIST 214.description: Introduction to the field of public history. Explores the challenges of portraying history in museums, parks, and other public history venues.
HIST 214.subject: HIST
HIST 214.title: The Practice of Public History

HIST 215.description: A survey of the beliefs and practices associated with the demonic and the Devil from c 500 B.C.E. to the 20th century.
HIST 215.subject: HIST
HIST 215.title: History of the Devil

HIST 216.description: An exploration of the evolution of global practices related to enforcing conformity with societal norms. Examines legal codes, philosophies, and technological devices associated with crime and punishment throughout history.
HIST 216.subject: HIST
HIST 216.title: History of Crime and Punishment

HIST 217.description: An examination of sports from their origins in the military preparedness of the ancient world to the entertainment and recreation of modern society, including their interactions with race, class, gender, sexuality, nationalism, amateurism, and professionalism.
HIST 217.subject: HIST
HIST 217.title: History of Sport

HIST 218.description: Introduction to the interdisciplinary field of food studies and historical approaches to the study of food.
HIST 218.subject: HIST
HIST 218.title: History of Food

HIST 220.description: An introduction to the transnational history of the Latin American diaspora, including U.S. Hispanics and Latinos/as/xs in the Western hemisphere.
HIST 220.subject: HIST
HIST 220.title: Introduction to Latinx History

HIST 300.description: The nature of historical evidence, the formulation of historical questions, the process of historical research, and the construction of historical arguments using primary sources and secondary materials.
HIST 300.subject: HIST
HIST 300.title: Introduction to the History Major: The Historian’s Craft

HIST 301.description: The formation of ancient Near Eastern cultures, the ultimate synthesis of these cultures and the resulting establishment of the Near East as an historical entity.
HIST 301.subject: HIST
HIST 301.title: The Ancient Near East to 323 B.C.

HIST 302.description: The origins and development of Greek civilization in its political, economic, social, and cultural aspects with special attention being given to the early and late classical periods and the Hellenistic Age.
HIST 302.subject: HIST
HIST 302.title: Greek History and Civilization to 146 B.C.

HIST 303.description: The origins of Rome and shaping of its republican government, the spread of Roman rule in Italy and across the Mediterranean, the establishment of the principate and formation of one diverse imperial society and culture.
HIST 303.subject: HIST
HIST 303.title: Roman Republic and Early Empire

HIST 304.description: Political, social and religious transformation of the Mediterranean world, 2nd to the 8th century., including the rise of Christianity, the decline of Roman power, and the rise of Islam.
HIST 304.subject: HIST
HIST 304.title: Late Antiquity: Imperial Rome to Islam

HIST 305.description: Representations of antiquity in cinema, television, and other contemporary media, with emphasis on Hollywood’s reception of Greek and Roman history.
HIST 305.subject: HIST
HIST 305.title: Greece and Rome in Film and Popular Culture

HIST 306.description: Topics include the formation of monarchies, the rise of Christianity, learning and universities, knighthood and social orders, and heresy and crusades.
HIST 306.subject: HIST
HIST 306.title: Medieval Europe, ca. 300-1492

HIST 307.description: Explores the concerns and importance of families in pre-modern Europe. Topics include household furnishings and management, social classes, gender roles, family law, marriages, business, children, feuds, and sexuality.
HIST 307.subject: HIST
HIST 307.title: Family and Society in Europe, c. 1200-1700

HIST 308.description: Practices of, reactions against, and ideas surrounding magic and witchcraft during the late Middle Ages and the time of Europe's Great Witch Craze .
HIST 308.subject: HIST
HIST 308.title: Magic and Witchcraft in Europe, c. 1200-1700

HIST 309.description: Social, cultural, and artistic movements in Italy and northern Europe from the Black Death (c. 1350) to religious reforms and revolutions (c. 1520).
HIST 309.subject: HIST
HIST 309.title: Age of Renaissance

HIST 310.description: Religious, social, and political reforms from the rise of local religious protests (c. 1450) to the crisis of the 17th century. The rise of Protestantism and reactions in Catholicism.
HIST 310.subject: HIST
HIST 310.title: Age of the Reformation

HIST 311.description: A survey of European political, economic, and intellectual development from the age of Louis XIV to the eve of the French Revolution.
HIST 311.subject: HIST
HIST 311.title: The Age of Absolutism, 1648-1789

HIST 312.description: The changes in France and Europe during the revolutionary decade, the rise of Napoleon, and the establishment of French hegemony over the Continent.
HIST 312.subject: HIST
HIST 312.title: French Revolution and Napoleon

HIST 313.description: Intellectual and cultural history of the Enlightenment with particular attention to its relationship with the colonial world and its challenges to eighteenth-century states. Readings focused on primary sources.
HIST 313.subject: HIST
HIST 313.title: The Enlightenment

HIST 314.description: History in video games; comparison of selected games with historical scholarship, to assess the validity of the games’ presentations of historical developments and the value of games to the understanding of history.
HIST 314.subject: HIST
HIST 314.title: Video Games and History

HIST 315.description: Athenian History from Persian Wars through Peloponnesian War.
HIST 315.subject: HIST
HIST 315.title: Rise and Fall of the Athenian Empire

HIST 316.description: Political, social, economic, and intellectual developments from 1815-1900, which brought European culture to its zenith and contributed to Europe's global domination.
HIST 316.subject: HIST
HIST 316.title: Nineteenth-Century Europe

HIST 317.description: The Great War, revolution, and reconstruction; the rise of authoritarian and totalitarian regimes and the coming of World War II.
HIST 317.subject: HIST
HIST 317.title: Contemporary Europe from World War I to World War II

HIST 318.description: The Second World War and its origins; the Cold War; European recovery; a divided continent and Europe in the Global Era.
HIST 318.subject: HIST
HIST 318.title: Europe from World War II to the Present

HIST 320.description: A survey of the political, social, economic, and cultural development of the British Isles from pre-history to the Restoration of 1660.
HIST 320.subject: HIST
HIST 320.title: The History of Great Britain I

HIST 321.description: A survey of the political, social, economic, and cultural development of the British Isles since 1660.
HIST 321.subject: HIST
HIST 321.title: The History of Great Britain II

HIST 323.description: Examination of the British Empire, tracing various historical themes as regions of world fell under British control, with particular attention to Ireland, India, and sub-Saharan Africa (especially South Africa) in the 17th Century-20th Century.
HIST 323.subject: HIST
HIST 323.title: The British Empire

HIST 324.description: Exploration of varied forms of servitude in the ancient and medieval Mediterranean; examination of human bondage in the Hebrew Bible, ancient Greece, Roman society, late antique religious teachings, and medieval Christian and Islamic societies; study of ancient slavery in modern political debates, historians’ writings, and television and film.
HIST 324.subject: HIST
HIST 324.title: Slavery and Freedom in the Ancient and Medieval World

HIST 325.description: The political, religious, and military developments within the Eastern Empire including its influence on Western and Slavonic Europe and Islam.
HIST 325.subject: HIST
HIST 325.title: Byzantine History: 4th to 11th Centuries

HIST 326.description: The political and military developments within the Eastern Empire from the invasion of the Seljuk Turks to its final destruction by the Ottoman Turks.
HIST 326.subject: HIST
HIST 326.title: Byzantine History: 11th to 15th Centuries

HIST 327.description: Holy war and realpolitik in Mediterranean East-West relations from the 10th through the 15th centuries with emphasis on the role of the crusades in the cultural formation, development, and international relations of East and West.
HIST 327.subject: HIST
HIST 327.title: The Crusades

HIST 328.description: The political, economic, and social developments in Great Britain and Ireland during the Victorian Age.
HIST 328.subject: HIST
HIST 328.title: Nineteenth-Century Britain

HIST 329.description: The political, economic, and social developments in Great Britain and Ireland during the 20th century.
HIST 329.subject: HIST
HIST 329.title: Modern and Contemporary Britain

HIST 331.description: The social, cultural, economic, and political life of black people in the United States to 1865.
HIST 331.subject: HIST
HIST 331.title: Black Experience in the United States to 1865

HIST 332.description: The social, cultural, economic, and political life of black people in the United States since 1865.
HIST 332.subject: HIST
HIST 332.title: Black Experience in the United States since 1865

HIST 333.description: A political and social history from the Bourbon Restoration to the present.
HIST 333.subject: HIST
HIST 333.title: France Since 1815

HIST 334.description: The earliest life on the steppe, the Kievan State, the foundations of Moscow, and the Russian empire to the reign of Nicholas I.
HIST 334.subject: HIST
HIST 334.title: The History of Russia from the Earliest Times to the Mid-19th Century

HIST 335.description: The decline of Imperial Russia, the Revolution of 1917, Lenin, Stalin, and the Soviet Union since Stalin.
HIST 335.subject: HIST
HIST 335.title: The History of Modern Russia and the Soviet Union

HIST 336.description: Imperial and Soviet foreign and military policies in the 19th and 20th centuries.
HIST 336.subject: HIST
HIST 336.title: Russian and Soviet Diplomatic History

HIST 337.description: Political, economic, social, and cultural development of the USSR from the 1917 Bolshevik revolution until the end of Stalin’s rule.
HIST 337.subject: HIST
HIST 337.title: Stalinism

HIST 338.description: A survey of German history including political, cultural, social, and economic developments from unification in 1871 to the present.
HIST 338.subject: HIST
HIST 338.title: Modern Germany

HIST 342.description: An introductory survey of the civilization of the Slavic peoples. The historical traditions and culture of the peoples that occupy much of the Eurasian continent.
HIST 342.subject: HIST
HIST 342.title: The Slavs in History

HIST 343.description: Nineteenth-century eastern European states and peoples; the political and social forces leading to World War I.
HIST 343.subject: HIST
HIST 343.title: The Fall of the Eastern European Empires

HIST 344.description: Survey of states in East-central and Southeastern Europe. Problems of national identity, modernization, and small state politics. Impact of WWII, the Cold war, the fall of communism, and the return to pluralism.
HIST 344.subject: HIST
HIST 344.title: Eastern Europe Since WWI

HIST 347.description: The impact of modern civilization upon the Middle East, including the history of the Arab, Turkish, Iranian, and Israeli segments of the Middle East during the 19th and 20th centuries.
HIST 347.subject: HIST
HIST 347.title: The Middle East in Modern Times

HIST 348.description: A survey of French North Africa (Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia) and Libya under colonial rule. The creation, development, and triumph of the nationalist movements, with particular attention to Algeria and its revolution.
HIST 348.subject: HIST
HIST 348.title: North Africa from Colonialism to Revolution: 1830-1962

HIST 349.description: Political, social, and economic history of the Middle East and North Africa in the years since World War II.
HIST 349.subject: HIST
HIST 349.title: The Contemporary Middle East and North Africa

HIST 350.description: Exploration of how and why Africa is often represented as helpless, the colonial origins of common patterns of development and humanitarianism, and other possible models for these processes.
HIST 350.subject: HIST
HIST 350.title: Saving Africa: Development and Humanitarianism in Historical Perspective

HIST 351.description: Social, cultural, economic, and political developments, focusing on internally and externally generated changes.
HIST 351.subject: HIST
HIST 351.title: Africa to 1800

HIST 352.description: Commercial and religious revolutions of the 19th century, imposition and ending of formal colonial rule, and post-colonial issues.
HIST 352.subject: HIST
HIST 352.title: Africa since 1800

HIST 353.description: Independent readings and written papers on appropriate topics.
HIST 353.subject: HIST
HIST 353.title: Problems in the History of Africa South of the Sahara

HIST 354.description: Surveys modern development of East Asia from 1800 to the present.
HIST 354.subject: HIST
HIST 354.title: Modern East Asia

HIST 355.description: Political, economic, social, and intellectual transformations of late imperial China from the Ming dynasty (1368-1644) through the last empire of China, the Qing dynasty (1644-1911).
HIST 355.subject: HIST
HIST 355.title: Late Imperial China

HIST 356.description: Introduction to the major social, economic, and political changes in China from the Communist Revolution in 1949 to the present.
HIST 356.subject: HIST
HIST 356.title: China Since 1949

HIST 357.description: The growth of the ancient state and the evolution of the samurai class and its political authority.
HIST 357.subject: HIST
HIST 357.title: Japan to 1800: Aristocrats and Warriors

HIST 358.description: The development of modern Japan: political evolution, industrial growth, social change, war, defeat, and occupation.
HIST 358.subject: HIST
HIST 358.title: Japan since 1800

HIST 359.description: Survey of the history of the Korean peninsula since 1945 in the context of the Cold War.
HIST 359.subject: HIST
HIST 359.title: Cold War Koreas

HIST 360.description: Global and comparative environmental-historical investigation of the ecological, socioeconomic, and cultural significance of wilderness protection, nature conservation, national parks, and nature tourism; field excursions required.
HIST 360.subject: HIST
HIST 360.title: Into the Wild: Global Conservation since 1800

HIST 361.description: In-depth study of the history, literature and culture of the Greek world era of Alexander the Great.
HIST 361.subject: HIST
HIST 361.title: The Age of Alexander the Great

HIST 362.description: Historical, literary, and cultural study of the Roman Empire during its final years of dominance in the West.
HIST 362.subject: HIST
HIST 362.title: The Fall of the Roman Empire

HIST 363.description: Historical, ethical and epistemic development of science and technology in its relationship to society.
HIST 363.subject: HIST
HIST 363.title: Science, Technology and Society

HIST 365.description: East Africans’ contributions to an Indian ocean World that transcends single nation-states (stretching from Mozambique and Somalia to the Middle east, India and China) from the deep past to the present, including sections on “piracy,” Islam, slavery, race, and gender.
HIST 365.subject: HIST
HIST 365.title: East Africa and the Indian Ocean World

HIST 367.description: Causes, consequences, and legacies of the largest mass displacement in modern history: the division of British India into independent states of India and Pakistan. Focuses upon British imperialism, South Asian nationalisms, religious identity, mass violence between Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs, and how these events are remembered.
HIST 367.subject: HIST
HIST 367.title: 1947 Partition of India and Pakistan

HIST 368.description: Study of Rome’s imperial family from Julius Caesar until the death of Nero.
HIST 368.subject: HIST
HIST 368.title: The Caesars: Rome's First Family

HIST 369.description: History of capitalist economic behavior and culture in various premodern societies: the Ancient Middle East, Classical Greece, the Roman Empire, early Islamic society, medieval Christian and Islamic states, the Mongol period and the era of global expansionism; evaluation of competing theories about premodern economic life and the meaning of capitalism
HIST 369.subject: HIST
HIST 369.title: History of Capitalism 1: Ancient and Medieval World

HIST 370.description: A history of capitalism and its evolving definitions in Europe from the Middle Ages to the 20th Century, including its role in agriculture, mechanical industry, international trade, and colonialism and domination.
HIST 370.subject: HIST
HIST 370.title: History of Capitalism 2: From the Industrial Revolution to the Global Economy

HIST 371.description: The evolution of airpower from the early 20th Century through the early 21st Century. The emphasis is on the development of various theories about the application of aerial force, and how operations in time of war have confirmed or challenged these theories from a multinational perspective.
HIST 371.subject: HIST
HIST 371.title: History of Airpower

HIST 372.description: The evolution of sea power through the development of steam navies around the globe, 1860 CE - 2020 CE.
HIST 372.subject: HIST
HIST 372.title: History of Modern Sea Power

HIST 373.description: An examination of the concept of freedom from its ancient origins to modern debates over free speech.
HIST 373.subject: HIST
HIST 373.title: History of Freedom

HIST 374.description: A comparative examination of the origins and development of nationalism and its impact on the modern world.
HIST 374.subject: HIST
HIST 374.title: Nationalism: Myth and Reality

HIST 375.description: German and Italian political movements; emphasis on the role of leadership, propaganda, and ideology. Fascist movements in France, Rumania, Hungary, and Great Britain.
HIST 375.subject: HIST
HIST 375.title: Nazis and Fascists in European History, 1919-1945

HIST 376.description: Thematic examination of the nature and impact of total war on European society; emphasis on socio-economic, cultural, and military aspects.
HIST 376.subject: HIST
HIST 376.title: War and European Society, 1914-1945

HIST 377.description: Capitalism in the Western world; the rise of modern corporate enterprise in Europe and America since 1850.
HIST 377.subject: HIST
HIST 377.title: Business in Historical Perspective

HIST 378.description: Social and cultural impact of urbanization in Europe since 1789 through a comparison of major cities such as London, Paris, Vienna, and Berlin.
HIST 378.subject: HIST
HIST 378.title: Urban Experience in Modern Europe

HIST 379.description: Survey of women in European history from the eighteenth to the twenty-first century. Focus on women’s citizenship beginning with Enlightenment idea of rights through developments in modern feminism.
HIST 379.subject: HIST
HIST 379.title: Women in Modern Europe

HIST 380.description: Introduction to Nazi Germany’s systematic mass-murder of Europe’s Jews and other minorities during war. Examination of forces that led to the Holocaust, including scientific racism, Nazi policy implementation, and dynamics of annihilation during war.
HIST 380.subject: HIST
HIST 380.title: History of the Holocaust

HIST 381.description: Modern history through the lens of the Nobel Peace Prize. Limitations of the Nobel as encouragement to peace.
HIST 381.subject: HIST
HIST 381.title: The Nobel Peace Prize: Peace, War, and Politics

HIST 382.description: A survey of the history of premodern medicine. How Western cultures of the past approached health and illness; anatomy; nutrition; sexuality; disease and plague; mental and emotional health; and more. From ancient Greece, through medieval and early modern Islamic, Jewish, and Christian approaches to medicine and the body.
HIST 382.subject: HIST
HIST 382.title: History of Medicine: Antiquity to the Scientific Revolution

HIST 383.description: The religious, cultural, social, and political conditions that shaped the Jewish experience in the Near East and Europe from Late Antiquity to 1500.
HIST 383.subject: HIST
HIST 383.title: Jewish History I: Late Antiquity to 1500

HIST 384.description: Case studies of Jewish history in Europe, America, and the land of Israel, 1500 to the present.
HIST 384.subject: HIST
HIST 384.title: Jewish History II: 1500 to the Present

HIST 385.description: Critical epochs in the spread of Christianity. Consideration of the great crises that shaped the structure and form of Christianity during the last 20 centuries: the Hellenistic world; the medieval syntheses; the breakup of Western Christian unity; the transition to worldwide mission activity in the industrial age.
HIST 385.subject: HIST
HIST 385.title: The Expansion of Christianity

HIST 386.description: The religious, political, social and economic institutions and intellectual and scholarly traditions developed by Muslim societies throughout Afro-Eurasia from late antiquity to the present.
HIST 386.subject: HIST
HIST 386.title: Islamic Institutions and Traditions

HIST 387.description: Representative messianic movements, millenarian visionaries and apocalyptic imaginings in the Islamic world from the 7th century to the present, with attention to related developments in the Jewish and Christian traditions over the last two millennia.
HIST 387.subject: HIST
HIST 387.title: Messiahs, Mystics and Rebels in the Islamic World

HIST 388.description: Historical investigation of kabbalah, a philosophical system and mystical current common to Judaism, Islam, and Christianity, from the medieval period to the present; focus on its formative role in early modern Western cosmology and science, and its ecological implications today.
HIST 388.subject: HIST
HIST 388.title: Kabbalah: Science, Religion and Nature in Western History

HIST 389.description: Occultism as a link between science and religion and its central role in Western intellectual and cultural history; the historical development of the science-magic-religion continuum in the Islamo-Christian world from late antiquity to present.
HIST 389.subject: HIST
HIST 389.title: Science, Magic and Religion

HIST 390.description: History of engineering practices, professions, and sciences, as well as development of engineered artifacts from the Middle Ages to the present.
HIST 390.subject: HIST
HIST 390.title: Engineering in History

HIST 391.description: The history of the computer; how it acquired various forms through the 20th century; how information, as defined by computers, had shaped the world over the past century.
HIST 391.subject: HIST
HIST 391.title: Information Technology: Past and Present

HIST 392.description: The history of physics, chemistry, geology, and related sciences since the Scientific Revolution.
HIST 392.subject: HIST
HIST 392.title: Making Modern Science: The Physical Sciences

HIST 393.description: The study of the life from antiquity to the present. Investigates the origins of modern biology and medicine and how life has shaped scientific, political, and economic thought.
HIST 393.subject: HIST
HIST 393.title: Making Modern Science: The Life Sciences

HIST 394.description: Evolution of the automobile from a conceptual idea through the present-day. Emphasis on analysis of the automobile's impact on culture, economics, the environment, politics, science and technology, and society.
HIST 394.subject: HIST
HIST 394.title: History of the Automobile

HIST 395.description: A survey of biopolitical, social, economic, and cultural aspects of epidemic diseases throughout world history.
HIST 395.subject: HIST
HIST 395.title: Plagues and Societies in World History

HIST 396.description: A history of tactics, strategy, weapons, and logistics from 500 B.C. to A.D. 1400.
HIST 396.subject: HIST
HIST 396.title: Evolution of Warfare I

HIST 397.description: A history of tactics, strategy, weapons, and logistics from A.D. 1400 to the present.
HIST 397.subject: HIST
HIST 397.title: Evolution of Warfare II

HIST 398.description: An interdisciplinary examination of sustainability around the world from social, environmental, technological, and economic perspectives from early times to the present.
HIST 398.subject: HIST
HIST 398.title: Sustainability in World History from Early Times to the Anthropocene

HIST 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
HIST 399.subject: HIST
HIST 399.title: Independent Study

HIST 400.description: Survey of the urban history of the United States from the 19th Century through today.
HIST 400.subject: HIST
HIST 400.title: Urban America in the Modern Age, 19th Century-present

HIST 401.description: The founding of the English colonies, their developing maturity, the events leading to the Revolution, and the creation of a new nation.
HIST 401.subject: HIST
HIST 401.title: The Development of the American People to 1789

HIST 402.description: The new republic and the developing democratic spirit in politics and culture.
HIST 402.subject: HIST
HIST 402.title: The New Nation, 1789-1828

HIST 403.description: The three cultures of East, South, and West; their interactions and the events leading to the Civil War.
HIST 403.subject: HIST
HIST 403.title: The Sections and the Nation, 1828-1860

HIST 404.description: The political, military, and social history of the War and the reorganization which followed.
HIST 404.subject: HIST
HIST 404.title: Civil War and Reconstruction, 1860-1877

HIST 405.description: A survey of recent United States history with emphasis on the economic, social, and literary developments from 1877 to 1917.
HIST 405.subject: HIST
HIST 405.title: The Rise of Industrial America, 1877-1917

HIST 406.description: The United States and a World at War, 1917-1945.
HIST 406.subject: HIST
HIST 406.title: The United States and a World at War, 1917-1945

HIST 407.description: A survey of the political, economic, social, and cultural developments in the period from World War II until the end of the 1960s era.
HIST 407.subject: HIST
HIST 407.title: United States History from World War II to the 1960's

HIST 408.description: This course is a survey of social, political, economic, and cultural developments since the 1960s. Students will develop a historical framework for exploring the rights revolution that began in the sixties and seventies, economic changes and transformations, trends in popular culture, the evolution of the media and communication technologies, America’s place in the world.
HIST 408.subject: HIST
HIST 408.title: The Making of Contemporary America: United States History, the 1960s to the Present

HIST 409.description: A study of South Carolina origins and developments.
HIST 409.subject: HIST
HIST 409.title: The History of South Carolina, 1670-1865

HIST 410.description: A survey of recent South Carolina history with emphasis on social and institutional development.
HIST 410.subject: HIST
HIST 410.title: History of South Carolina Since 1865

HIST 413.description: A survey of Canadian development from colony to modern nation.
HIST 413.subject: HIST
HIST 413.title: History of Canada

HIST 415.description: Historical exploration of the daily lives and personal stories of Americans through biographies and ethnographies.
HIST 415.subject: HIST
HIST 415.title: Voices of America: U.S. History Through Biography

HIST 416.description: Experiences of Native people in North America from the period before European colonization through the 21st Century.
HIST 416.subject: HIST
HIST 416.title: Histories of Native America

HIST 420.description: The establishment and consolidation of the Spanish and Portuguese empires in the Western hemisphere; interaction of Indians, Africans, and Iberians, and the formation of social, economic, and political traditions in Latin America; political independence.
HIST 420.subject: HIST
HIST 420.title: Colonial Latin America

HIST 421.description: Traditional society in the area and problems arising from social, economic, and political changes since independence; comparative studies of national responses to these problems.
